newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end down on Brazil basis, Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end down on Brazil basis, Taiwan.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures closed mostly lower and soyoil ended down on news Taiwan passed on two soybean tenders and on a decrease in the weekly crush pace which coincided with lower cash basis in Brazil, traders said.

"When the crush came out at the low end of expectations, that set the tone for the overnight (Project A trade)," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities. "There was pretty good cash movement and the basis came under pressure. On top of that, the basis yesterday afternoon and this morning in South America was under pressure."
Thursday's NOPA crush rate of 28.12 million bushels was below expectations for 28.5 million to 29.5 million bushels.

Taiwan overnight passed on a 54,000-tonne tender for South American soybeans and a joint U.S. corn/soybean tender just one day after announcing a ban on pork exports due to an outbreak of foot and mouth disease there.
Traders in Taiwan attributed the passed tenders to a cutback in feed demand linked to an imminent cut in Taiwan's hog herd because of the outbreak.
Soymeal closed $2.90 per ton lower to $0.80 higher with May down $2.90 at $277.40. Soyoil closed 0.40 to 0.20 cent per lb lower with May off 0.37 at 24.40.
Domestic cash soymeal basis levels were up Friday with brokers quoting a slight increase in demand in reaction to the lower crush.

But while the reduction meant tighter supplies, some floor sources speculated world demand would fall just as sharply. They cited reports soymeal basis levels in Brazil had fallen on Thursday as harvest there reached full tilt.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought 600 lots May soymeal, Merrill Lynch bought 700 May and Lind-Waldock sold 300 May, traders said.
In soyoil, ADM bought 300 May and 50 December while Cargill bought 250 May, traders said, while Iowa Grain sold 400 May and 200 July and Refco Inc bought and sold 300 May.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 25,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 33,948 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 15,000 lots, against Thursday's 19,289.
